newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak flood damage seen at SKK two bln -ministry.
newsitem.headline: Slovak flood damage seen at SKK two bln -ministry.

text.p: Heavy rains and flooding over the past week in Slovakia have caused some two billion crowns ($58.3 million) worth of damage to property, crops and agricultural output, the Ministry of Agriculture said on Tuesday.

"These are just the first rough estimates. We have to wait with the final calculation until the flood waters recede," ministry spokeswoman Anna Majkutova told journalists during a regular government session.
"But the disaster should not affect supplies of basic commodities to the local market. The losses so far appear not to warrant the need to import basis commodities," she added.
On Tuesday, Agriculture Minister Peter Baco was quoted as saying that as much as one-third of Slovakia's 1997 grain harvest may be lost as the result of heavy rain and flooding.
Last week the Slovak Statistical Bureau (SUSR) estimated the 1997 grain harvest would yield up to 3.12 million tonnes, an increase of 19.1 percent over 1996.

Rain and floods are reported to have delayed the harvest in southern Slovakia, the country's granary. Only some 1,500 hectares, or 0.81 percent out of total 190,017 hectares of sown grain has so far been harvested in the southern region.

Several Slovak rivers have over the past week reached their highest water levels in the past 100 years, but the country appers to be much less affected by floodings than its western and northern neighbours, the Czech Republic and Poland.
